chunks: As for what Saʿd narrated from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl ibn Bazīʿ, who said:
I asked Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام about salat (prayer) in a garment of brocade, and he said: So long as there are no images in it, there is no objection.

So the first point regarding this report is that we have already narrated from Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام that which conflicts with this narration, and it is not permissible for his statements to differ except for a valid aspect or a sound interpretation. Moreover, the apparent wording of the report does not indicate that there is no objection in every circumstance; so when that is not the case in it, we interpret it as applying to the state of الحرب rather than the state of choice, and that is indicated by what follows.

key_terms.التَّمَاثِيلُ: images or figures depicted on the garment
key_terms.الصَّلَاةِ: salat (prayer), the ritual act whose ruling is being discussed
key_terms.الِاخْتِيَارِ: the state of normal choice or ordinary circumstance
key_terms.الْحَرْبِ: the condition of war, to which the report is being restricted
key_terms.الْخَبَرِ: the report or narration under examination
key_terms.تَأْوِيلٍ: interpretive reconciliation used to harmonize differing reports
key_terms.ثَوْبِ: garment or clothing worn during prayer
key_terms.دِيبَاجٍ: brocade, a fine silk fabric under legal discussion here

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on praying in a brocade garment according to this narration from Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This report addresses the legal ruling of performing salat (prayer) in a garment of dībāj (brocade). The compiler notes that other narrations from Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام differ from this report, so this narration is interpreted in a restricted way, applying to a state of war rather than ordinary voluntary circumstances.
